doc.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Where jazz can go next
summary: Jazz risks becoming a museum piece; he names Dave Douglas and the Knitting Factory crowd as innovators.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Jazz has moved awful fast in its history it seems like.
And I’m constantly wondering where can it go from here? I mean it’s been through the electronic end of it.

Well I mean there’s a lot in musical terms that could be developed that hasn’t been in terms of even harmony in terms of extended forms, compositionally, I mean there’s a whole lot of things that could be done. And it is being done and it will be done and all that, but I think that this at particular moment that’s not what’s really being focused on. You know it’s more kind of the attitude seems to be we’re going to take a breather from all of this because all the crazy — because the innovation was getting too crazy and too removed from the audience. So now it’s time to just kind of retrench and establish an audience or institutionalize jazz, concentrate on its classic history and all that. And that’s fine, you know, that’s great. But you have to be careful that it doesn’t go the way of classical music and just become a museum piece. It’s got to be living, it’s got to be new, it’s got to be daring, it’s got to be innovative too.
To help to grab a young audience.

Well yeah, yeah. And that’s happening. I mean there are players like Dave Douglas, you know a very fine trumpet player who is really starting, just beginning to get the attention he deserves, and he’s kind of associated with that Knitting Factory crowd, which has been kind of on the fringe, but some of that stuff is getting very sophisticated, some of the musicians who do it are terrific and they’re really doing some interesting things. I mean that’s just to name one example, I mean there are other people around too.
